evidence_new.identifier: arXiv:2503.18709 (v2, 2025-07); OpenReview QL9bKc9p3U (MICCAI 2025); CoRR 2025 version SrKGUdmmYb
evidence_new.title: Revisiting Automatic Data Curation for Vision Foundation Models in Digital Pathology (Chen, Vincent-Cuaz, et al.)
evidence_new.design: Tile-level automatic curation of a 350M-tile pool: hierarchical k-means tree on UNI tile embeddings (Vo-style, k-means++ and resampling), then top-down balanced sampling from the tree. Compares curated subsets with random batches (BR) vs stratified batches (BS) across tree configurations, subset sizes (10%, etc.), and against full data with random batches (F-BR), supervised WSI-class curation (S-BR, S-BS).
evidence_new.dataset: Digital pathology tiles; RoI-level linear probing on BACH, BreakHis, CRC-type sets, BRACS, PCAM; WSI-level 9 clinical tasks from two centers.
evidence_new.baseline: F-BR (full data, random batches); supervised curation S-BR, S-BS.
evidence_new.result: Partial extraction. Curated data with RANDOM batches (T1-BR, S-BR) gives the LOWEST average performance. Curation + STRATIFIED batches (T-BS) gives the top average, followed by S-BS and F-BR. With 10% subsets from different trees, stratified batch sampling consistently outperforms random, e.g. T-BS 82.2% average bACC (tree T1, level 3) vs 82.0% for other trees. Authors describe a size-balance trade-off in curated subsets and recommend allocating samples inversely to bottom-cluster volume (uniform sampling from T1 at level 4). Differences between top configurations are small (~0.2 pp in the passage read).
evidence_new.which_class: Not per-class; bACC averaged over tasks.
evidence_new.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (method section 2, results passages, conclusion). Table values not fully read.
evidence_new.limitation: Digital pathology, 350M tiles, UNI embeddings, linear probing on frozen features. Not a continued-training study. Effects are small. Authors list bottom-level informative sampling and batch construction as open.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: This is a medical-domain validation of the Vo-style hierarchical curation (E1 extended). It changes our experiment design: a dataset-level sampler with random batches (our WeightedRandomSampler and the X1 plan as written) reproduces their worst configuration (curation + random batches). Batch-level stratification by cluster is the piece to test. Corrects the earlier claim in ssl-recent.json that no medical application of Vo curation was found.

evidence_new.title: Enhancing Skin Lesion Classification Generalization with Active Domain Adaptation
evidence_new.label_free: partial: continued SSL is label-free; the pipeline then fine-tunes with labels and applies active DA, which uses labels on target-domain queries
evidence_new.design: DINO (ResNet-50, from natural images) retrained with SSL on all available skin lesion datasets (label-free), then supervised fine-tuning on source labels, then active domain adaptation on target data. Five random seeds.
evidence_new.dataset: Ten skin lesion datasets (dermoscopy), source/target domain shift.
evidence_new.baseline: ImageNet-SL init; prior UDA baseline BSP reported in [10]; SL vs SSL-pretrained comparison.
evidence_new.result: Partial extraction. Authors state SSL retraining on in-domain skin data is an effective UDA method, outperforming the cited baseline on 9 of 10 target domains (worse on BLH). Mean and std over 5 seeds reported in tables not extracted.
evidence_new.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (abstract, introduction, method, training section).
evidence_new.limitation: DINO ResNet-50, not ViT. Uses labels downstream and active DA queries. Domain-shift framing rather than minority-class recall. Single SSL seed per the passages read (not verified).
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: The closest dermatology precedent for our exact step: continued DINO-style SSL on pooled skin-lesion data with no labels, then a label-using readout. Supports the premise of our pipeline. Does not test our imbalance endpoints.

evidence_new.title: The Bad Batches: Enhancing Self-Supervised Learning in Image Classification Through Representative Batch Curation
evidence_new.design: Batch curation for SSL: selecting representative batches rather than uniform random batches during image SSL.
evidence_new.result: Abstract not retrieved (crossref metadata only). Not used for numbers.
evidence_new.limitation: No abstract or full text in hand.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: Directly on batch construction, the component E11 says matters. Obtain the paper through the user's institutional access or a Zotero copy before relying on it.

evidence_new.title: Mini-Batch Optimization of Contrastive Loss
evidence_new.design: Theory: mini-batch InfoNCE optimization equals full-batch only when all mini-batches are used; proposes selecting high-loss mini-batches via spectral clustering to speed SGD convergence.
evidence_new.result: Abstract only: proposed selection outperforms vanilla SGD in their experiments.
evidence_new.limitation: Batch selection by loss needs per-sample losses each step, costly in MoCo. Not tested on medical or imbalanced data.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: Alternative batch-construction principle. Lower priority than cluster-stratified batches; noted for the synthesizer.

evidence_new.title: Gradient Cluster Imbalance: Why Large Batches Favor Normalized Optimizers
evidence_new.design: Theory: per-sample gradients form nearly orthogonal clusters with imbalanced sizes; plain GD progresses slowly on rare clusters; normalized optimizers (SignGD, Muon) mitigate this.
evidence_new.dataset: Language and vision models (measured per layer).
evidence_new.result: Abstract only. Structural assumptions; partial measurement support.
evidence_new.limitation: Unpublished, anonymous submission. Optimizer-level, not sampler-level. Supports the mechanism behind cluster-size reweighting but does not test it.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: Theory support for cluster-balanced sampling (rare clusters get slow progress). Do not cite as established. Mechanism motivation only.

evidence_new.title: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
evidence_new.design: JEPA predictive loss plus SIGReg (sketched isotropic Gaussian regularization). Claims no stop-gradient, no teacher-student, no schedulers; single trade-off hyperparameter.
evidence_new.result: Abstract only: ViT-H/14 linear eval 79% on ImageNet-1k.
evidence_new.limitation: General-domain claims; not tested on dermatology or minority recall. Replacing our MoCo objective is a large change and breaks comparability with every historical arm.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: Candidate objective swap, low priority for this phase. Note the claimed stability across hyperparameters as a possible answer to our SSL-hyperparameter fatigue, but it is an abstract-level claim.

evidence_new.title: A Graph Matching Approach to Balanced Data Sub-Sampling for Self-Supervised Learning
evidence_new.design: Title only in our results; abstract not retrieved.
evidence_new.relevance_to_us: Potential balanced-subsampling alternative to the cluster sampler. Needs a non-anonymous route to the text.

experiment_changes.change: SPLIT into two arms. X1a: hierarchical balanced sampler with random batches (current plan as written). X1b: same hierarchical clusters, but with STRATIFIED batch construction (each batch of 16 draws across clusters, e.g. one or more samples from distinct top clusters, leaf-level stratification if top level has fewer than 16 clusters with enough items).
experiment_changes.why: E11 (pathology, MICCAI 2025): curation with random batches was the worst configuration; curation with stratified batches was best. X1a alone risks reproducing the weak arm.
experiment_changes.priority: X1b is the arm to run first. X1a is the control for the batch effect. Both replace PhA alpha arm B.
experiment_changes.risk: Stratified batches in MoCo change the in-batch negatives distribution (more diverse negatives, fewer same-cluster negatives). Log the same-component collision rate per batch (brief audit baseline 0.49%).
experiment_changes.expected_effect: Still small. The E11 differences are about 0.2 pp bACC between top configurations. Subjective probability of a seed-consistent melanoma recall gain: about 30-35%.
